name: Revenue recognition
description: ASC 606, schedules, adjustments and period close.

cards.title: Five steps
cards.body: ASC 606 and IFRS 15: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the price, allocate it, recognize revenue. Zenskar identifies obligations from the products and features in each phase.
cards.example: A subscription plus onboarding gives two obligations.

cards.title: Over time or at a point
cards.body: Subscriptions and managed services are recognized over time; deliveries and milestones at a point in time.
cards.example: A delivery is recognized on delivery.

cards.title: Distribution methods
cards.body: Over-time obligations get a baseline schedule: straight-line, usage-based (tied to consumption) or entitlement-based (credits, milestones, features).
cards.example: $12,000 per year straight-line is $1,000 per month.

cards.title: Adjustment methods
cards.body: When reality changes, a revised schedule is built by front-load (next open period, required for material changes above 5%), straight-line over remaining periods, or back-load (final period).

cards.title: Monitoring and audit
cards.body: Zenskar watches for scope changes, usage variance, variable consideration and FX. Each adjustment keeps its rationale, approval workflow and audit trail.
cards.example: Usage overshoots forecast, so the schedule is revised.

cards.title: Ledger objects
cards.body: Chart of accounts, accounts, journal entries and lines, balance sheet and income statement.
cards.example: A journal entry per recognized amount.

cards.title: Period close
cards.body: Validate period close returns a checklist without closing. Closing then locks the period: no transactions inside it can be modified.
cards.example: Validate March, fix gaps, then close.

edgeCases: Separate clocks. Recognition dates are independent of invoice and payment dates.
The 5% rule. Material adjustments above 5% are front-loaded.
Closed means closed. After closing, nothing in the period can change, so always validate first.
Not legal advice. Zenskar does not assess whether a contract is legally enforceable or replace accounting judgment.
Entitlements. They are off-balance-sheet and not reconciled with financial transactions.
Version note. Accounting was reorganized in the newer docs; confirm what your tenant has enabled.

quiz.question: Which method fits a usage-priced service?
An adjustment is 8% of the contract. Which method is required?
What does back-load do?
options: Defers to the final period when outcomes are certain

quiz.question: Before closing a period you should…
quiz.explanation: Validation returns a checklist without closing.

quiz.question: Does revenue follow the invoice date?
quiz.explanation: Recognition depends on performance, not billing.

qa.question: Billing vs revenue recognition?
qa.answer: Billing is what you charge and when. Revenue is when you have earned it.

qa.question: Straight-line vs usage-based vs entitlement-based distribution?
qa.answer: Straight-line spreads evenly, usage-based follows consumption, entitlement-based follows credits, milestones or features.

qa.question: Front-load vs straight-line vs back-load adjustment?
qa.answer: Front-load books the change in the next open period, straight-line spreads it over remaining periods, back-load defers it to the last period.

qa.question: Over time vs point in time?
qa.answer: Subscriptions are recognized over time; deliveries and milestones at a point in time.

qa.question: Validate vs close a period?
qa.answer: Validate returns a checklist without closing. Close locks the period.

qa.question: Journal entry vs journal line?
qa.answer: An entry groups lines that make the accounting posting.

qa.question: Balance sheet vs income statement?
qa.answer: Position at a date versus performance over a period.

qa.question: Entitlement vs recognized revenue?
qa.answer: Entitlements are usage rights, off-balance-sheet, and not reconciled to revenue.

qa.question: Annual subscription revenue?
qa.answer: Straight-line over the term.

qa.question: Metered consumption contract?
qa.answer: Usage-based distribution.

qa.question: Scope increases 10% mid-term?
qa.answer: Material (above 5%), so front-load.

qa.question: Month-end close?
qa.answer: Validate, fix gaps, then close the period.

qa.question: Milestone-based service?
qa.answer: Entitlement-based distribution.

qa.question: Material threshold?
qa.answer: Adjustments above 5% must be front-loaded.

qa.question: Can I edit a closed period?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: Is a legally unenforceable contract flagged?
qa.answer: No. Zenskar does not assess legal enforceability or replace accounting judgment.

qa.question: Does the invoice date move revenue?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: What if usage overshoots the forecast?
qa.answer: Monitoring flags the variance and an adjustment schedule is proposed with rationale and approval.

qa.question: What are the five steps?
qa.answer: Identify the contract, identify obligations, determine the price, allocate it, recognize revenue.

qa.question: How are obligations identified?
qa.answer: From the products and features configured in each phase.

qa.question: What is kept for audit?
qa.answer: Rationale, approval workflow and an audit trail for each adjustment.
